chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who killed a man by error during the Sacred Month. He said: 'The wergild is intensified upon him, and upon him is the emancipation of a neck, or fasting two consecutive months from the Sacred months.' I said, 'Supposing something enters into this?' So he said: 'What is it?' I said, 'The day of Eid and the days of Tashreeq?' He said: 'He should fast them, for it is a right that is obligatory upon him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for accidental killing during the Sacred Months?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific expiation for accidental homicide committed during the Sacred Months, emphasizing the aggravation of blood money and the obligation of freeing a slave or fasting two consecutive months. Notably, it clarifies that the prohibition of fasting on Eid and Tashreeq days does not exempt the individual; rather, these days are counted within the two-month period, reflecting the Shia juristic view that the obligation remains binding despite the temporary impediment. This ruling underscores the continuity of divine duties even when specific conditions, such as sacred months, introduce additional weight or minor restrictions.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who kills a man in error during the Sacred Month. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The wergild is harsh upon him, and upon him is the emancipation (liberation) of a neck, or Fasting two months consecutively from the Sacred months’. I said, ‘Supposing something enters into this?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What would it be?’ I said, ‘A day of Eid, and days of Al-Tashreek (11<sup>th</sup>, 12<sup>th</sup> and 13<sup>th</sup> of Zil-Hijja)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would Fast these, for it is a right necessitated upon him’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri’ab from Zurarah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who kills a person by mistake in a sacred month. He (the Imam) said, ‘Blood money has become substantial on him. He is required to set a slave free or fast for two consecutive months of the sacred ones.’ I then asked, ‘What happens if something takes place in between?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Give an example.’ I said, ‘If ‘Id day or the days of tashriq (11, 12, and 13) come in between. He (the Imam) said, ‘He is required to fast because it is a binding right upon him.’”
